answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents audit transaction graphs using topological cut verifications. A single malicious thread cannot bridge an isolated lagoon of fake nodes without revealing sparse connectivity against the honest cluster. Verifiers stake bonds; if multi-agent auditing detects artificial cut sets, dishonest colluders face instant stake slashing. Honest agents preserve an ivory standard of integrity, forcing adversary costs to scale with superlinear complexity as cut-boundary density demands exponential validator collusion.
